requirements.requirement: On node1, /tmp is mounted with nosuid, nodev, and noexec, and the setting survives reboot.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, /tmp was an active, enabled tmpfs mount with nosuid,nodev,noexec, and direct execution failed with rc=126. After the observed reboot, the mount remained enabled and active with the same options, execution was still denied, and its persistent systemd drop-in was present.

requirements.requirement: On node1, /dev/shm is mounted with nosuid, nodev, and noexec, and the setting survives reboot.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, /dev/shm showed nosuid,nodev,noexec and direct execution failed with rc=126. After reboot, the live mount retained all three options, execution remained denied, the persistent fstab entry was present, and fstab verification reported no errors or warnings.

overall_summary: Both mount-hardening outcomes are satisfied and directly verified across a real reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: the healthy pre-restart boot ID 4d842549-003e-4f78-bb26-12732f129e58 was recorded, the reboot was acknowledged, the post-restart ID changed to 11ba681e-75d9-41b8-87dd-424042931598, and the system returned to running with no failed units and both hardened mounts recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: nosuid and nodev were verified through live mount flags before and after reboot, but their kernel behavior was not separately exercised with a setuid executable or device node. The live flags are nevertheless direct evidence of the requested mount semantics.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc, so retention of /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening is inferred directly from its creation and the absence of any later removal command.

operational_hygiene.summary: The configuration, remount, enablement, execution probes, cleanup, reboot, and recovery checks all had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles. Test scripts were removed. One minor unnecessary retained mutation is the backup /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening created during the edit and not shown removed; it is low-risk but constitutes residual clutter. No failed services, package damage, or new network exposure was observed after execution.
